chunks: As for those whose souls are taken by the angels (at death) while in a state of unbelief, they will be asked by the angels: "What (state) were you in?" They will answer: "We were oppressed in the land." And the angels will say: "Was not God's earth large enough for you to migrate?" Their abode will be Hell, and what an evil destination!

key_terms.تَوَفَّاهُمُ الْمَلَائِكَةُ: those whose souls are taken by the angels

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of 'ظَالِمِي أَنفُسِهِمْ' and the angels' question about migration in this verse?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is often interpreted as addressing the Muhajirun who remained in Mecca or Medina, highlighting that physical inability must be genuine to excuse one from migration (Hijrah). The angels' question, 'Was not God's earth spacious?', underscores the principle that spiritual obligation requires proactive effort, and mere weakness does not absolve one of the duty to seek a place where faith can be practiced. This serves as a foundational lesson for the Shia community regarding the balance between enduring oppression and actively seeking religious freedom.
